chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
If there is a grove (of fish) wherein there are no reeds, something from the fish is taken out, so whatever is in the grove can be sold.

key_terms.أَجَمَةٌ: A natural enclosure or grove, often referring to a place where fish are gathered or kept.
key_terms.قَصَبٌ: Reeds, used here to describe a specific feature of the enclosure that affects the ruling.

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for selling fish from a natural enclosure (ajamah) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling to clarify the permissibility of selling fish in a natural enclosure (*ajamah*) when the exact quantity is unknown (*mubahs*). The condition of 'no reeds' likely distinguishes this from enclosures where reeds might obscure visibility or indicate a different type of ownership structure, thereby allowing the seller to remove a sample to verify quality before sale. This reflects the Shia juristic approach to resolving uncertainty (*gharar*) in commercial transactions by ensuring the buyer can inspect the goods.

en.hubeali:
Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘If there is a grove wherein there are no reeds, something from the fish having been taken out, so whatever is in the grove can be sold’.
en.sarwar: 11. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If there is a bunch of trees without reeds with a few fish taken out along with what is in the bunch of trees, it can (lawfully) be sold.’”
